title: How Indian Shopify Stores Can Accept International Payments
summary: Enable international payments on Shopify in India. Compare gateway fees, check card activation, understand currencies and use the pre-launch payment checklist.
body_markdown:
Table of Contents


Toggle


If your Shopify store shows prices to your US buyer in dollars, make the currency clear when they’re finally checking out. If the checkout unexpectedly charges them in rupees, the change can create confusion and lead to an abandoned sale.


According to[Shopify’s help centre](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/international/pricing/limitations) , selling in buyers’ local currencies through Shopify checkout is supported by Adyen or Shopify Payments. Orders using other third-party payment providers are processed in your store’s default currency. Shopify Payments (Shopify’s own payment gateway) isn’t available in India. This means that you have to integrate[an approved third-party gateway](https://www.cashfree.com/shopify-payment-gateway-india/) to receive payments.


Besides that, under the[RBI export regulations](https://www.rbi.org.in/scriptS/NotificationUser.aspx?Id=13277&Mode=0) applicable from 1 October 2026, the usual realisation period is 9 months from shipment for goods or from invoice for services. Exports invoiced or settled in INR have a 12-month period. Your AD bank can consider extensions under the rules.


So, it’s high time that you set up your international payments the right way, starting with your gateway.


### TL;DR


Indian Shopify stores need a supported third-party provider to accept online international payments. Confirm export payment approval, the buyer’s payment currency and INR settlement terms. Shopify’s transaction fee is separate from the gateway fee, and plugin installation alone does not activate overseas payments.


##


Why Your Shopify Store Needs a Cross-Border Payment Gateway


Since you can’t collect money from your overseas customers via Shopify Payments, you connect a third-party payment gateway to your store. For international orders, a non-bank provider aggregating cross-border payments needs the applicable RBI authorisation as a cross-border payment aggregator (PA-CB).


A PA-CB is a payment company that RBI has authorised to process cross-border payments for the online businesses it signs up. Under RBI’s Master Direction on Payment Aggregators, a PA-CB can process[up to ₹25 lakh per transaction](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_ViewMasDirections.aspx?id=12896) . If you sell high-value products, you might need to check your prices against this cap.


##


How to Choose a Shopify International Payment Gateway in India


Shopify charges a separate transaction fee on eligible orders paid through a third-party gateway, and that rate depends on your Shopify plan. Shopify’s India pricing page lists:


**Shopify plan** **Shopify’s fee per order (third-party gateway)**


Basic 2%


Grow 1%


Advanced 0.60%


Plus 0.20%


These fees are separate from the gateway’s processing fee. Compare the combined cost, applicable GST, currency conversion charges, refunds and chargeback fees before you choose a gateway. Check these five things:


- **RBI licence:** Verify the provider’s RBI authorisation and confirm that it covers inward cross-border payments for exports.
- **Currencies:** Check how many currencies your buyers can pay in, and distinguish Shopify checkout currency from any currency conversion offered on the gateway’s payment screen.
- **Settlement time:** Ask how many days the gateway takes to deposit rupees into your Indian bank account.
- **Compliance records:** Confirm that the gateway gives you a record for every international payment. You need these records to reconcile your GST filings.
- **Shopify app:** Confirm that the gateway has a native Shopify app, so you can connect it without a developer.

##


Shopify International Payment Checklist: Documents and Store Policies


Before you can switch on your international payments, your gateway will verify your business, and you’ll need some important documents. Here’s a list of the ones that you’ll need to show.


### KYC Documents


These are the basic[KYC documents](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/documents-required-for-payment-gateway-in-india/) that you may need, depending on your business type:


- Your PAN
- Aadhaar or another government-issued ID
- A Shop and Establishment certificate, Udyam registration or other accepted business proof
- A cancelled cheque or bank statement
- Your GST certificate, where applicable


If you run a private limited company or LLP, you may also need your company PAN, Certificate of Incorporation, MOA and AOA (or LLP Agreement), a board resolution, and the PAN and ID of directors, partners or beneficial owners, as applicable.


### Export Registrations


If you export physical goods, make sure that your business has the applicable registration with the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT). Plus, check how you’ll handle export taxes with your accountant. Review these documents:


- **Import Export Code (IEC):** This is the 10-character alphanumeric code that you receive from DGFT for a[₹500 application fee](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/what-is-import-export-code-iec/) , subject to application validation. If you export services, you generally don’t need an IEC unless you claim Foreign Trade Policy benefits.
- **GST Letter of Undertaking (LUT):** Exports are zero-rated supplies under GST. Eligible registered exporters can use an LUT to export without payment of IGST, subject to the applicable conditions. A bond or the payment-and-refund route may apply in other eligible cases; the absence of an LUT does not mean that every exporter must pay IGST on every export. You can file your LUT on the[GST portal](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/gst-login-password-portal-guide/) in Form GST RFD-11. Please note that you have to file it every financial year.


### Website Pages


Cashfree’s team audits your website before activating your account. According to[Cashfree’s onboarding rules](https://www.cashfree.com/docs/help/onboarding-related/onboarding-faqs) , your store must show:


- Terms and conditions, About us, and Privacy policy pages
- A Contact us page with an email ID and a valid phone number
- Your registered business name
- Refund, shipping, and pricing pages, if your business model needs them


### What You Can’t Sell


- Cashfree doesn’t onboard businesses that sell drop-shipped merchandise, alcohol, or tobacco.
- Cashfree’s banking partners may not approve international cards for some sectors, such as gambling, dating, and alcohol.
- Cashfree’s published documentation lists checkout restrictions for buyers in Belarus, Cuba, Iran, Sudan, Syria, Russia, Iraq, Pakistan, and Afghanistan. Recheck region restrictions before targeting a market.


##


How to Enable International Payments on Shopify: Step-by-Step Setup


Once your documents are ready, the setup takes five steps.


### Step 1: Sign Up and Complete KYC


Create an account with your gateway and upload your documents.


Cashfree states that account activation takes 24 to 48 working hours after document verification. International payment methods may require additional review. Until then, you can try the dashboard in Cashfree’s test environment.


### Step 2: Request International Payment Methods


To do so, go to Settings > Payment Methods in your Cashfree dashboard and check the available[international payment methods](https://www.cashfree.com/accept-international-payments/) , including international cards, Apple Pay, and PayPal. Request or connect the supported methods for your account and Shopify integration. Cashfree’s onboarding team then reviews your business with its banking partners before it turns these methods on.


### Step 3: Install the Gateway’s Shopify App


If you already use Cashfree, just log in with your existing credentials and your account settings carry over. If you’re new, go to Settings in your Shopify admin > Click Payments > Add payment method, and just install your gateway’s[Shopify app](https://www.cashfree.com/docs/help/payments/integrations/integrations) . Authorise the connection and activate the provider in Shopify’s payment settings.


### Step 4: Decide Which Currency Your Buyers Pay In


With Cashfree’s[Pay Native](https://www.cashfree.com/docs/payments/international-payments/ipg/pay-native) , your buyer can choose to pay in *their* local or home currency at the rate shown on the payment screen, and you’ll still receive it in rupees. Cashfree converts the currency at its own checkout. This is separate from Shopify’s local-currency checkout. Confirm Pay Native availability for your Shopify setup, including the buyer’s currency choice and conversion markup.


### Step 5: Test Before You Go Live


Place a few test orders using the test mode supported by your Shopify integration, and check that all your policy pages are live. Verify successful, failed and cancelled payments, the currency shown, and the return to your Shopify order confirmation. Test the[refund process](https://www.cashfree.com/docs/help/end-customer/refunds) and confirm that Shopify and the gateway show matching payment status. Then switch your gateway to live mode after activation. It’ll help you know if you’re getting blocked somewhere in the system and can fix it before your customers face an issue.


##


Get Your Store Ready for Shopify Overseas Payments


Shopify Payments isn’t available in India, so your payment gateway setup needs to address three things: the currency your overseas buyers pay in, what each order costs you, and how fast the money reaches your bank. So, make sure you choose the right one.


Before your first overseas order, confirm international card activation, the buyer’s payment currency, your total fees and the documents you’ll receive. Keep invoices, payment records and settlement reports together for reconciliation.

##


FAQs About Shopify International Payments in India


#### **1. How can you accept international payments in India?**


Connect an RBI-authorised cross-border payment gateway to your website or Shopify store. Your buyers pay by international card, Apple Pay, or PayPal where supported. Confirm the settlement arrangement for each method; PayPal payments may settle directly through PayPal. For bank transfers from overseas clients, Cashfree’s[Global Collections](https://www.cashfree.com/docs/payments/global-collections/introduction) is a separate invoice-based collection option; it is not the Shopify card checkout flow.


#### **2. Does Shopify provide a payment gateway in India?**


Shopify Payments isn’t available to businesses based in India. Indian stores use a third-party gateway, and Shopify charges them a fee of 0.2% to 2% per order, depending on the plan.


#### **3. What documents are required to use a payment gateway in India?**


You need your PAN, a government-issued ID, business registration proof, bank account proof, and your GST certificate where applicable. Your website must also be live, with terms, privacy, and contact pages. Confirm the full list of documents for your business type during onboarding.


#### **4. Which international payment gateways can Indian businesses use?**


Use a gateway that RBI has authorised as a cross-border payment aggregator for exports. You can check a gateway’s status on RBI’s list of authorised payment system operators.


#### **5. Do you need a US company to accept international payments on Shopify?**


No. Cashfree offers Pay Native to eligible businesses registered in India that have a valid website or app. You accept international cards through your Indian business and receive rupees, subject to approval and the supported Shopify integration.


#### **6. Can you charge international customers in USD on Shopify from India?**


Shopify’s local-currency checkout is supported through Shopify Payments or Adyen. With other gateways, Shopify processes orders in your store’s default currency. Cashfree’s Pay Native can offer home-currency payment on its own payment screen where enabled. Confirm the end-to-end Shopify flow before promising USD checkout.


#### **7. Do you need an IEC to sell abroad on Shopify?**


Yes, if you sell physical goods.[DGFT](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/dgft-portal-login-iec-registration/) issues the IEC for a ₹500 application fee, subject to validation and applicable exemptions. If you export services, you generally don’t need one unless you claim Foreign Trade Policy benefits.


#### **8. What is a FIRS?**


A Foreign Inward Remittance Statement (FIRS) is a record of an international payment you received. Cashfree provides FIRS records for international payments. Use them alongside invoices and bank records for applicable GST reconciliation and RBI reporting. A FIRS does not itself replace an eBRC or close an EDPMS entry.


#### **9. How long do you have to receive payment for an export?**


Under the rules applicable from 1 October 2026, the usual period is 9 months from shipment for goods or invoice for services. Exports invoiced or settled in rupees get 12 months. Special cases and AD-bank-approved extensions may apply; confirm the deadline with your bank. Receiving an INR credit after a gateway converts foreign-currency proceeds does not by itself establish that the export is INR-settled under these rules.


#### **10. What is the maximum amount per international transaction?**


A cross-border payment aggregator can process up to ₹25 lakh per transaction under RBI’s rules.


#### **11. Can you sell dropshipped products internationally through Cashfree?**


No. Dropshipped merchandise is on Cashfree’s list of prohibited categories.
